summary: Unapplied hourly buffer credit after cross-region fallback during large embedding batch
description: Customer reports they did not receive hourly buffer credits for a large batch embedding job that partially failed over from us-east to eu-west. The job was billed at hosted rates for the eu-west portion instead of consuming the customer's reserved hourly buffer, resulting in an unexpected charge spike. Customer provided invoice lines and job IDs.
impact: Customer VeloxSearch saw a $3,100 unexpected charge on their monthly invoice. Their job was a high-volume nightly embedding run; immediate credit is requested while we investigate. Business impact: potential churn risk for a dedicated customer with committed capacity.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer ran a scheduled batch embed job (job_id: job-20250217-0741) targeting 'embedder-v2-large' pinned to their dedicated pool.
2) At 07:41 UTC, the dedicated pool reported a GPU allocation failure in us-east-1; scheduler triggered fallback routing to eu-west-1 for remaining shards.
3) Postback stream sent two sets of usage records: one with reserved-hour tags and another with hosted-rate tags after failover.
4) Billing reconciler appears to have accepted hosted-rate postbacks and ignored reserved-hour buffer offsets for the eu-west segment.
logs: customer-provided invoice excerpt: INV-2025-02-VEL-114 (charged hosted rate for 1.2M embed tokens)
postback payload snippets (sanitized): postback_id pb-87f3, timestamp 2025-02-17T07:42:12Z, tags: [reserved_hour:pool-velox-12, region:us-east-1]
failover postback: postback_id pb-87f4, timestamp 2025-02-17T07:43:03Z, tags: [region:eu-west-1, route:fallback, billing_rate:hosted]
billing-reconciler log: reconcile-run 2025-02-17T08:10Z accepted pb-87f4 and applied hosted price; note: no matching reserve-debit found for pb-87f4
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: postback ordering led reconciler to treat eu-west fallback as standalone hosted usage because reserved-hour offset record from us-east arrived after the fallback postback (race condition).

Checked reconciler tombstones: found delayed reserve-debit message (reserve-debit id rd-559) arriving at 07:45Z, after reconcile window for pb-87f4. Reconciler currently applies a 2-minute window to match reserve debits to usage events.

Observed that scheduler forwards fallback shards with billing_rate:hosted when cluster-level reservation flag was not propagated during failover. Edge-case in scheduler: reservation context lost when controller reassigns to cross-region pool.
Customer reports they had 3 reserved hours available; logs confirm reserved-hour balance before job start. No prior refunds or credits applied.
comments: Support (Tom Erickson) 2025-02-18: Thanks for the report — we've ingested the billing artifacts and started a reconciler trace. Tagging billing-eng and infra-scheduler.

Billing Eng (Lina Park) 2025-02-19: Trace shows reconcile-run skipped the delayed reserve-debit. We can run a manual correction to apply the reserved buffer to pb-87f4 segment. Need approval for provisional credit prior to automated fix.

SRE (Marco Ruiz) 2025-02-19: Root cause appears to be scheduler not including reserve_context header on cross-region reassign. PR to set header on failover in progress: github.com/redwood-inference/scheduler/pull/1296.
Customer (VeloxSearch - Emma Liu) 2025-02-19: Appreciate the quick investigation. Requesting provisional credit while fix rolls out — this overcharge affects month-end reconciliation.
resolution: Pending manual credit application. Billing team to issue provisional invoice credit of $3,100 to VeloxSearch and mark as provisional in accounting. Engineering to deploy scheduler fix (PR 1296) to ensure reserve_context is preserved during cross-region failover. Post-deploy reconcile job to reprocess the affected day's postbacks to validate future reconciliation. Follow-up: run a 48-hour monitoring job to ensure no further orphaned hosted charges for reserved pools.
